newsitem.title: TURKEY: SOCCER-TURKISH CLUB SEEK TO JAIL REFEREE OVER DENIED PENALTY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TURKISH CLUB SEEK TO JAIL REFEREE OVER DENIED PENALTY.

text.p: Turkish club Besiktas have applied to an Istanbul court demanding the jailing for three years of a referee for denying them a crucial penalty in their goalless draw against lowly Vanspor.
It is the first such case in Turkish soccer history.

Club lawyer Necati Toker said in remarks reported on Saturday that referee Metin Tokat had abused his job as an unbiased public worker in refusing to give Besiktas a penalty after a Vanspor player "clearly handled the ball in the penalty area" to block a Besiktas free kick.
Lawyer Toker said in his application to the court that Tokat should be given a three-year jail sentence for abusing his position.
The match was played last weekend. Besiktas are fourth in the league with 39 points. Vanspor are 16th with 14.
